findings.quote: These formulas work for any angle from $0^\circ$ to $360^\circ$, and the signs come out correctly by themselves.
findings.problem: The lesson defines sine and cosine only for an acute angle of a right triangle ("Take a right triangle and one of its acute angles"). It then applies them to any angle and works Example #8 with $20\cos150^\circ\approx -17.32$, but never explains what the cosine of an angle over $90^\circ$ means or why it is negative there. It names no prerequisite either, although the unit-circle lesson (lesson-trigonometry-unit-circle) teaches reference angles and quadrant signs. A student who knows only SOH-CAH-TOA cannot see where the negative sign comes from, and cannot get the value without a calculator. The brief also says general quadrant direction needs more than right-triangle sine and cosine.
